recipes.name: Giant Onigiri inspired by Cooking from Valkyries
ingredients: 1 water (enough to cover rice to the first knuckle)
instructions: For the Rice
Rinse 6 cups of short-grain rice until the water runs clear. - 6 cups short grain rice (uncooked)

Rice Cooker: Add rice to the rice cooker, cover with water until it reaches the first knuckle when you dip your finger in. Cook on the normal rice setting. - 6 cups short grain rice (uncooked) - 1 water (enough to cover rice to the first knuckle)

Stovetop Rice: In 2 large pots, cook 3 cups of rice in each, covering with the water using the first-knuckle methodd. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook until all water is absorbed (about 15-20 minutes). - 6 cups short grain rice (uncooked) - 1 water (enough to cover rice to the first knuckle)
Once cooked, transfer all the rice into a large tray or bowl to cool. Let it rest until it reaches room temperature.
For the Salmon Filling
Rub salmon filets with sake to freshen them up, then coat generously with salt on all sides. - 3 salmon filets - 2 tbsp sake - 2 tbsp salt
Place salmon filets in the fridge for 39 minutes to allow the salt to draw out moisture. - 3 salmon filets
After 30 minutes, pat the salmon dry and place them on a foil-lined baking tray. - 3 salmon filets
Bake at 450°F for 15 minutes, or until the salmon is cooked through and slightly firm. - 3 salmon filets
Once the salmon has cooled slightly, flake it with a fork into small chunks, but don't mash it. Set aside. - 3 salmon filets
For the Tuna Mayo Filling
Drain cans of tuna and transfer to a small mixing bowl. - 5 2 oz cans of tuna, drained
Add Kewpie mayonnaise and stir until well combined. The tuna should be creamy but still have texture. Set aside. - ½ cup Kewpie mayonnaise
For the Umeboshi Filling
Remove the pits from Umeboshi plums and chop them into small chunks. - 5 ½ Umeboshi (Japanese salted and pickled plums)
Set aside in a small bowl. This will be the third filling.
For the Assembly
Line 2 large bowls with plastic wrap, ensuring there's enough overhand to lift the rice later.
Divide the cooled rice equally between the two bowls. Use your hands to press the rice down gently, forming a flat surface. - For the Rice
In one bowl, create a shallow crater in the middle of the rice. Fill it with flaked salmon. - 3 salmon filets
In another bowl, create another crater and fill it with the tuna mayo mixture. - 5 2 oz cans of tuna, drained
Using the plastic wrap, carefully lift the rice from one bowl and place it on top of the other, sandwiching the fillings together to form a large, round onigiri. - For the Rice
Gently press down to secure both halves. The plastic wrap will help you shape it without rice sticking to your hands.

Lay out your sheets of Nori. Carefully press them onto the giant rice ball, covering the entire surface. The warmth and moisture from the rice will help the Nori adhere. - 5 large sheets of Nori (seaweed) - salted water (for shaping)
If needed, cut smaller pieces of Nori to match any uncovered areas. The goal is 100% Nori coverage. - 5 large sheets of Nori (seaweed)
Slice the giant Onigiri in half to reveal the layers of filling.
Serve immediately, cutting into smaller portions for each person.
